tasks.short: Research repertoire, develop a new interpretation and restage the work with a recorded staging plan.

steps.what: Retrieve traditional dance references and the company's existing repertoire materials
Study traditional dances and interpret the source work's structure and context
outputs: artistic understanding of the source work

steps.what: Develop new interpretations and test movement possibilities with the company
inputs: artistic understanding of the source work

steps.what: Write the selected staging plan and changes to the repertoire version
Check and communicate the restaging choices while staging the work with performers

tasks.design: Configure repertoire identifiers, source links and a restaging-plan template in {DOCS}. Source interpretation and creation remain human, and writing the staging plan is separate from communicating and realising it with the company.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repertoire references and version changes can be difficult to retrieve and repeatedly describe.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document metadata and reusable staging headings can reduce mechanical preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Creating an interpretation that has artistic purpose and respects the source context.
tasks.human_edge: Embodied artistic judgement, cultural understanding and collaboration with performers.
tasks.altitude: Build a clearer record of the company's restaging choices while protecting creative work.

evidence.claim: Native archive metadata and document templates may reduce reference and layout effort; no digest case establishes a restaging labour benefit.

assumptions: The baseline includes the working staging plan as well as research, creative testing and staging; no plan write is concealed inside live collaboration.
The choreographer selects work identity in s1, supplies artistic interpretation in s2-s3 and records version changes in s4. Missing archive metadata is resolved manually with its effort retained.
Use the native archive view and document template before custom software. No model selects or generates the artistic interpretation.
The author's ordinary plan save is included at full effort without self-approval. The separate gate concerns the exact instructions communicated to performers.
Performers are internal company colleagues; no external publication or rights submission is assumed.
unknowns: Quality of the repertoire archive metadata
How often an existing plan layout can be reused
Rights and permissions applicable to the selected work
research_questions: Can one observed restaging reuse source links and plan headings while retaining the full artistic interpretation effort?

already_counted.description: Source interpretation, artistic development and live staging

incremental.description: Maintain repertoire links and plan headings

approvals.approved_version: The exact passage, staging choices and intended performers checked immediately before instruction; changed staging conditions require a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R95 gives5 gross minus1 upkeep =4 net. Low: source recordings lack comparable version metadata and the plan is bespoke, leaving retrieval14.5 and writing9.5 plus75 creative work, R99; net0. High: source links are reusable but interpretation notes remain specific, leaving retrieval13 and writing9 plus75, R97; net2 after1 upkeep. Creative development and staging are retained in full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Maintain a traceable repertoire archive while leading artistic reinterpretation personally.
reach: Help rehearsal assistants trace repertoire versions
role.ambitious_version: A choreographer with clearer continuity between historical repertoire and new company interpretations.
